figures.caption: Figure 7.9.3 shows the latch and DA limiting amplifier schematics. The latch outputs are buffered by double emitter followers with feedback to reduce transient ringing effects, and preamplified by Q1,2. Grounding the (common) bases of the transistors in the final output stage extends the collector-emitter breakdown voltage of Q11,12 to near BVCBO. A differential output voltage swing beyond 10V could therefore be realized by adding more DA cells and extending the output line. references.sentence: A block diagram of the modulator driver prototype is shown in Fig. 7.9.1.
The I and Q clocks are generated by a frequency doubler followed by a quadrature divide-by-two circuit (see Fig. 7.9.2) [3].
Figure 7.9.3 shows the latch and DA limiting amplifier schematics.
An RLC model fits the measured output return loss data well as seen in Fig. 7.9.4.
The 2.8mm2 prototype (including bondpads, see Fig. 7.9.7) is implemented in IBM’s 0.18μm SiGe-BiCMOS 7WL technology (BVCEO = 3.3V).
Figure 7.9.5 shows the measured single-ended (SE) output waveforms and eye patterns for 231-1 length NRZ data at 10Gb/s through 10cm of semi-rigid coax, a DC block and 20dB attenuator.
Total rise/fall time (20-to-80%, including output interconnections) is 15ps (min), and can be increased to 50ps (max) by varying the latch clock phases digitally (see Fig. 7.9.5).
Figure 7.9.6 compares the prototype driver’s performance with (III-V) commercial products and recently published designs.
